pr_title: Fix the ICU time format conversion logic
pr_body:
Revise the ICU time format conversion logic to support all unquoted literal texts and the `B` and `b` pattern symbols.

Fix #103592
pr_comments:
I'm new to such a big and complex project and not sure how to test these changes, so this is a draft at the moment. Looking forward to help from anyone.

Example affected patterns:

| ICU pattern | Result (Old) | Result (New) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a नि h:mm` | `tt  h:mm` | `tt नि h:mm` |
| `ཆུ་ཚོད་h:mm:ss a` | `h:mm:ss tt` | `ཆུ་ཚོད་h:mm:ss tt` |
| `ཆུ་ཚོད་ h སྐར་མ་ mm a` | ` h  mm tt` | `ཆུ་ཚོད་ h སྐར་མ་ mm tt` |
| `Bh:mm:ss` | `h:mm:ss` | `tth:mm:ss` |

More information can be found in the fixing issue.

@PopSlime thanks for submitting the PR. 
Let's add a test case in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/System.Runtime/tests/System.Globalization.Tests/DateTimeFormatInfo/DateTimeFormatInfoLongTimePattern.cs to validate the implemented changes.
/azp run runtime-extra-platforms
Azure Pipelines successfully started running 1 pipeline(s).
@mkhamoyan Is it safe to assume those cultures use a 12-hour clock? `fr-FR` uses a 24-hour clock on my side.

> @mkhamoyan Is it safe to assume those cultures use a 12-hour clock? `fr-FR` uses a 24-hour clock on my side.

My bad, `fr-FR` shouldn't be there.

> How about this?

Looks good to me. 
> By the way, this fails on my PC (Windows) with `mi: 'h:mm:ss'` and `mi-NZ: 'h:mm:ss'`. Should we address this in another issue?

Yes , we should file an issue for that. 
Let's push in the PR and check how it behaves on other platforms.
@dotnet-policy-service agree

> By the way, this fails on my PC (Windows) with mi: 'h:mm:ss' and mi-NZ: 'h:mm:ss'. Should we address this in another issue?
> Yes , we should file an issue for that.

I don't think we can fix that as the patterns are picked from Windows. I suggest you mark your new test methods with the attribute and see if this can help? 

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7934e6449229c57f6c2d7ab9ea1688dc82cf95de/src/libraries/System.Runtime/tests/System.Globalization.Tests/DateTimeFormatInfo/DateTimeFormatInfoLongTimePattern.cs#L264
I'll do that, but I also want to see if similar issues are occurring on other platforms, so let's wait for these checks to be done.

>  this fails on my PC (Windows) with mi: 'h:mm:ss' and mi-NZ: 'h:mm:ss'.

I am trying on my machine, and I am not getting the same results you are getting. 

```
mi-NZ .. Maori (New Zealand) .. h:mm tt .. h:mm:ss tt
mi .. Maori .. h:mm tt .. h:mm:ss tt
```

running code like:

```C#
            var ci = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("mi-NZ");
            Console.WriteLine($"{ci.Name} .. {ci.EnglishName} .. {ci.DateTimeFormat.ShortTimePattern} .. {ci.DateTimeFormat.LongTimePattern}");
            ci = CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("mi");
            Console.WriteLine($"{ci.Name} .. {ci.EnglishName} .. {ci.DateTimeFormat.ShortTimePattern} .. {ci.DateTimeFormat.LongTimePattern}");
```

What Windows version do you have? I am wondering how you get this result?

It seems that the version of the CLDR data installed on my PC is below 36. The time format for `mi` was fixed in https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/pull/104.

- Operating system: Windows 10
- Version number: 22H2
- Internal version: 19045.4529

ok, then the attribute https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/7934e6449229c57f6c2d7ab9ea1688dc82cf95de/src/libraries/System.Runtime/tests/System.Globalization.Tests/DateTimeFormatInfo/DateTimeFormatInfoLongTimePattern.cs#L264 is not going to help. You may try using something like https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/2a779abce2a9dd8722dd3786aca1d09311990222/src/libraries/System.Runtime/tests/System.Globalization.Tests/NumberFormatInfo/NumberFormatInfoData.cs#L10 to avoid the failure. 

I meant using check like `if (PlatformDetection.ICUVersion.Major >= 68)` .

`fr-CA` is failing with the added test:

```
Bad short time pattern for culture fr-CA: 'HH h mm min'

Bad long time pattern for culture fr-CA: 'HH h mm min ss s'
```

Looks to me you have something wrong in parsing the single vertical quotes. The patterns should be `HH 'h' mm` and `HH 'h' mm 'min' ss 's'`

> Looks to me you have something wrong in parsing the single vertical quotes. The patterns should be `HH 'h' mm` and `HH 'h' mm 'min' ss 's'`

I tested these patterns and they are correctly converted with the logic.

This occurs only on the `browser-Release-wasm-Mono` platform, which seems to be using time formats from a source other than ICU and is not related to the conversion logic here. Should we address this issue later?

The incorrect patterns in the browser environment is caused by the following code, which does not handle literal strings and copies them into the pattern as is. Opening another issue to address it.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ab80b9af668601ebc102760b4c4e60d23ba8d8f/src/mono/browser/runtime/hybrid-globalization/culture-info.ts#L77

> I meant using check like `if (PlatformDetection.ICUVersion.Major >= 68)` .

That'll do, but should we fix the patterns for lower ICU versions despite it is an issue with the CLDR itself? If we do, how should we do that?

> Currently overriding the default time patterns with the following method in my own project, just for reference.

That is fine to do it in the app side. In .NET we have to honor whatever ICU/OS give us even if users think it is wrong. Fixing the time patterns need to raise to the ICU to fix.

@PopSlime the tests are still failing. For now, can you exclude running this test with hype globalization? or special case `fr-CA` when encountering it? @ilonatommy @mkhamoyan do you have any better suggestion? @PopSlime already logged issue to tracking fixing fr-CA formats.

issue_context.title: Incorrect general long time pattern for some cultures on Android
issue_context.body:
### Description

On Android, some cultures have an incorrect general long time pattern, causing `DateTime.ToString(IFormatProvider)` to produce badly formatted strings.

### Reproduction Steps

Consider the following code:

```cs
new DateTime(2000, 1, 1, 20, 0, 0).ToString(new CultureInfo("zh-TW"));
```

### Expected behavior

A correctly formatted string (like `2000/1/1 下午8:00:00`) is returned.

### Actual behavior

A badly formatted string `2000/1/1 8:00:00` is returned, in which a 12-hour clock is used without an AM/PM designator.

### Regression?

_No response_

### Known Workarounds

_No response_

### Configuration

- .NET version: 8.0
- Target operating system: Android
- Architecture: x64, arm64
- Android version: 13 (tested both on an emulator and a physical device)

### Other information

_No response_

I did some further investigations, this issue seems to be device-dependent. Just in case, this issue was reproduced with the `system-images;android-33;google_apis;x86_64` system image.

This issue seems to relate to this `ConvertIcuTimeFormatString` method.

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/b93061adc14eaaf5e83e366f9fba507ad917308c/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Globalization/CultureData.Icu.cs#L354

The current implementation does not cover the full Unicode [Date Format Patterns](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-dates.html#Date_Format_Patterns). In the case of `zh-TW` (which expands to `zh-Hant-TW` and inherits `zh-Hant`,) the pattern symbol `B` is used [1], which is not covered in the aforementioned method.

Please consider supporting or partially supporting as many pattern symbols as possible just in case.

[1] https://github.com/unicode-org/cldr/blob/3147eda09f19de58463cc80d64248071531500a0/common/main/zh_Hant.xml#L4963

Affected CLDR version: 40 and above (https://cldr.unicode.org/index/downloads/cldr-40#h.mc372kkefa0z)

Affected Android version: 13 and above (https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/resources/internationalization#versioning-nougat)

@PopSlime thanks for the update. We should support the `B` conversion. Are you interested in submitting a PR for that? 

CC @mkhamoyan
Hi, @tarekgh. I've submitted a PR for this issue but I'm not sure how to test it. Would you mind checking it out?

review_comments: Maybe easier to have `result[resultPos++] = '\'';` before reurning false and remove this from the calling site.

I am not sure what exactly you are trying to do. If pattern has `\` should be kept as it is inside the string and not escaping it by adding extra one. 

To handle parsing two adjacent single vertical quotes, you can simply check the next character when encountering a single quote. If it is another single quote, store the pair as `\'`. Thus, `''` will be converted to `\'` regardless of whether it appears inside or outside other quotes. This approach should simplify the necessary changes.
Backslashes are not used as part of escape sequences in the ICU format, so we need to duplicate them or they will be escaped in the .NET format.

ok, thanks.

Is there an example of any ICU pattern that uses backslash? I am curious to see such case.
There isn't but in case there will be such cases in the future.

> To handle parsing two adjacent single vertical quotes, you can simply check the next character when encountering a single quote. If it is another single quote, store the pair as `\'`. Thus, `''` will be converted to `\'` regardless of whether it appears inside or outside other quotes. This approach should simplify the necessary changes.

Agree. I'll work on that later.
Could you please add a little comment telling ICU formats don't have escaping so we need to escape `\` if we encountered any?
Should `b` be translated to `t` instead? I didn't look at specs yet to see what correct translation should be.
`b` is "am, pm, noon, midnight" and `B` is "flexible day periods," both of which should be acceptable to be translated to `tt` (AM/PM) as no other period is present in .NET if I'm not mistaken.

Looking at: https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/datetime/

|Symbol | Meaning | Pattern | Example Output
| -- | - | - | -
a | AM or PM | a, aa, or aaaaaaaaaaaa | PM [abbrev]PM [wide]p
| b | am, pm, noon, midnight | b, bb, or bbbbbbbbbbbb | mid.midnightmd
| B | flexible day periods | B, BB, or BBBBBBBBBBBB | at night [abbrev]at night [wide]at night [narrow]

It looks to me `b` and `B` is not directly translated to `AM/PM`. We need to think more how we can support that in the .NET.
True. But for now I think this is an acceptable solution.
I suggest closing this PR till we figure out how we translate these symbols. Thanks @PopSlime for trying to help with that. Let's continue the discussion on the issue.

> True. But for now I think this is an acceptable solution.

I am inclined to agree with that. This may be better than fully ignoring it.
